eSource@ENRON (40enron@enron.com) sent the most messages on 2001-09-05. I filtered the corpus for messages from that address in September 2001 and grouped them by UTC date. That gave 160 messages, and 23 of them were sent on the 5th. The next highest days were 2001-09-28 with 19 and 2001-09-14 with 16. I didn't open any individual messages, so the sources below are only the ones I could pull from the counts.

ANSWER: 2001-09-05
SOURCES:

Angelic Davis (angelic.davis@enron.com) sent 6 unique messages to dana.davis@enron.com between 2001-10-01 and 2001-11-01 (end exclusive). Dana Davis is in the To or Cc line of all six. I ran a metadata query on sender, recipient and date range, so each message appears once.

ANSWER: 6
SOURCES: Eec51ca95dc10, E78c208665714, Ea4671be47808, Ea9e43a0d11aa, Ef703ce92e611

Jeff Dasovich sent the most messages to Richard Sanders in that window. I filtered for messages sent to richard.sanders@enron.com (To or Cc) from 2001-05-29 up to but not including 2001-06-05. That gave 37 messages, and Dasovich sent 8 of them. Susan Mara was next with 5, then Janette Elbertson with 4.

I didn't cross-check for messages under other address variants for Sanders, so the count covers only richard.sanders@enron.com. The source IDs below are five of Dasovich's eight messages.

ANSWER: jeff.dasovich@enron.com
SOURCES: Ec64a0fe2fe15, Efbeffae21bed, Eb4461cb03bfd, E89c6a95fd0e2, Eaa28b1519008

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages in April 2001 to vkaminski@aol.com, with 173 unique messages. I counted a message once per address, whether the address was in To or Cc. I filtered to messages sent from vince.kaminski@enron.com, and 458 messages matched.

The next highest was vince.kaminski@enron.com, his own address, with 135. After that came shirley.crenshaw@enron.com with 54. I didn't open any messages to confirm their contents. The source ids below are the first three messages returned by the April 2001 filter. They aren't specifically messages to the AOL address.

ANSWER: vkaminski@aol.com
SOURCES: E1554858ab4b5, E72a31f377f27, E710caacc5ce1

trace.input: {"code":"const m=await corpus.messages({from:\"vince.kaminski@enron.com\",after:\"2001-04-01\",before:\"2001-05-01\",limit:5000});\nconst c={};for(const x of m){if(!x.from.toLowerCase().includes(\"vince.kaminski@enron.com\"))continue;for(const a of new Set([...x.to,...x.cc]))c[a]=(c[a]||0)+1;}\nconsole.log(m.length,Object.entries(c).sort((a,b)=>b[1]-a[1]).slice(0,5));console.log(m.slice(0,3).map(x=>x.id))"}

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages on 2001-04-25, with 47. The next highest were 2001-04-11 with 37 and 2001-04-27 with 36.

I counted messages sent from vince.kaminski@enron.com between 2001-04-01 and 2001-05-01, grouped by UTC date. The query returned 458 messages for the month. I didn't keep message ids from the run, so I have none to cite.

ANSWER: 2001-04-25
SOURCES:

The message is Ef817f5aac97c, "FW: 082501 Enron Confirmation", dated 2001-08-24. Bryant Frihart sent it. A search of the full text found only this one message with 703-227-8777. The number appears as "703.227.8777 Phone". The message went to hayhurstb@paceglobal.com, with Tammy Gilmore and C. Giron on cc.

ANSWER: bryant.frihart@enron.com
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c

The only message that mentions ORE-7509 is **E2083b9620d07**. It was sent on 2002-02-27 with the subject "(CMS-26) NOTICE OF INTENTION TO TRANSFER MEMBERSHIP".

The sender is marketing@nymex.com, shown as "Exchange Information @ENRON". The message was in the deleted_items folder of custodian shackleton-s. The matching line reads "Edward Orenchuk (ORE-7509)", so the reference appears to be a NYMEX membership identifier for Edward Orenchuk.

ANSWER: marketing@nymex.com
SOURCES: E2083b9620d07

All 29 matches were returned, so the count is complete.

14 distinct sender addresses sent at least one message containing "Raptor" between 2001-11-01 and 2001-11-30 UTC. I searched the full text of every message, headers included, case-insensitively. That gave 29 matching messages, and I counted the distinct senders among them after lowercasing the addresses.

ANSWER: 14
SOURCES:

The sender with the most messages containing "Azurix" between 2000-12-01 and 2001-01-01 (UTC) is enron.announcements@enron.com. A case-insensitive search of the full text and headers found 35 matching messages in that period. I counted them by sender. enron.announcements@enron.com sent 7. jeffrey.shankman@enron.com was next with 5.

ANSWER: enron.announcements@enron.com
SOURCES:

The most messages containing "Dynegy" were sent on 2000-05-23, with 14 of the 103 matching messages in May 2000. I found them with a case-insensitive grep over the full text of every message, headers included. The next highest days were 2000-05-04 and 2000-05-19, with 10 each.

ANSWER: 2000-05-23
SOURCES:

The message is E2093dccd9417, and Robin Barbe sent it from robin.barbe@enron.com. It was sent on 5 December 2000 to Chris Germany and Dick Jenkins, with the subject "PSEG Meeting". It mentions a meeting "on Tuesday, December 5, 3:00 p.m., in EB-2934."

A grep for "EB-?2934" matched 9 messages. Only this one uses the hyphenated form, "EB-2934". The other eight write it as "EB2934", and they are all conference room bookings. If you meant any spelling of the reference, those eight are also candidates.

ANSWER: robin.barbe@enron.com
SOURCES: E2093dccd9417

The only message that mentions 703-227-8777 is E f817f5aac97c. It was sent on 2001-08-24 by bryant.frihart@enron.com, and the number appears there as "703.227.8777 Phone". The number is written with dots, so an exact search for the dashed form found nothing. A looser pattern found it.

That sender sent 2 messages in August 2001 (UTC), counted by sender address.

ANSWER: 2
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c
